definition: A variant of group-relative policy optimization that operates at the sequence level rather than the token level, introduced to reduce the variance of the update. Neither source studies it directly; both use it to test whether a problem attributed to GRPO is really an estimator problem. In the subjective-verification study it is one of three algorithms applied to the same tasks -- alongside GRPO and a variant that removes length and standard-deviation normalization -- and its failure to rescue the mathematically strong model on three of four tasks is what licenses the paper's conclusion that reasoning collapse is a credit-assignment problem on tasks without a canonical correct trajectory rather than an optimization-bias artifact. In the entropy-dynamics work it appears in an analysis reducing whether an update raises or lowers entropy to the sign of one scalar per token. In this archive it therefore functions mainly as a control: a fix at the estimator level whose failure locates the problem elsewhere.

evidence.note: Shows on four internal Netflix verification tasks that explicit reasoning usually degrades subjective judgement, that applying RLVR to fix it makes the policy abandon deliberation for short heuristic guessing, and that a length bonus gated on answer correctness is what stops the collapse.
evidence.title: LLM Reasoning for Subjective Tasks: Failure Modes, Mitigation, and Dynamic Reasoning Routing

evidence.note: Reduces the question of whether an update raises or lowers entropy to the sign of one scalar per token, shows that under GRPO what matters is that scalar's deviation from a policy-weighted baseline rather than its own value, and proves the deviation averages to zero over a batch.
evidence.title: On the Entropy Dynamics in Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

name: GSPO
